name: comp-103

frames.best_why: The clean light pill shows both chevrons flanking the count with no cursor over it.

tagline: Up and down arrows bracketing a score in one rounded voting strip.
summary: A light fully-rounded pill split into three touching parts: a chevron-up button, a bold count and a chevron-down button. Hovering or pressing either end shades that section.
appearance: A wide white pill sits on a near-black stage, its three sections divided by faint seams and the outer ends fully round. A dark chevron points up on the left, the score "235" sits in bold in the centre, and a matching chevron points down on the right.
behaviour: Hovering either chevron darkens its section of the pill and pressing darkens it further, giving vote feedback; the count itself stays fixed. Once the pointer leaves, the pill returns to flat white.
use_when: Readers should push a visible score up or down with one tap, as on a forum post or comment.
avoid_when: The count is a fixed literal and the buttons have no click handler, so a vote never changes the number.
customise: Nothing is exposed as a prop: the score is a literal and neither button has an action, so wiring real votes needs a source edit.
weight_why: Three small static elements with only hover and press colour feedback.

a11y.note: Both ends are labelled Upvote and Downvote with focus rings, but nothing changes the score, so the control stays decorative.

issues: The count sits on the same white as the buttons, so it reads as a label rather than a badge.
polish_why: Clean grouped pill with clear press feedback; the count blends in and never changes.
